prompt: A right triangle has legs $6$ and $8$ and hypotenuse $10$. For the angle whose opposite side is $6$ and adjacent side is $8$, what is the tangent, as a decimal?
hint: TOA: Tangent is Opposite over Adjacent. The hypotenuse is not invited.

hints.text: TOA: Tangent is Opposite over Adjacent. The hypotenuse is not invited.
Opposite is $6$, adjacent is $8$, so tangent $= \frac{6}{8}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tangent is steepness
steps: Tangent is just rise over run — the slope of the slanted side.
The triangle rises $6$ while running $8$ across.
$6 \div 8 = 0.75$, so it climbs $0.75$ for every $1$ across.

alternativeExplanations.title: Shrink to the 3-4-5
steps: The $6$-$8$-$10$ triangle is a $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle doubled.
Same shape means the same angles and the same ratios.
